Nvidia's board of directors announced Sunday that it's launching an independent investigation following reports that CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a Chinese spy operation . Nvidia also published a message that Huang sent to the company admitting that he had an affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based chip company Megaspeed (though he didn't mention her by name). A memo circulating among U.S. policymakers earlier this year claimed that Alice Huang had been recruited by China's Ministry of State Security to spy on Nvidia's CEO. "I owe my family and all of you an apology," Jensen Huang wrote. "I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry." Huang added that he'd "fallen short" of his responsibility to the company. "To my colleagues at NVIDIA, including those I have worked alongside for decades, and to our board, partners, and shareholders around the world: you deserve better from me," he said. As the AI race between the United States and China heats up , chips, especially Nvidia's chips, have been a major focus . Huang also seems to have a close relationship with President Donald Trump , who's been a cheerleader of the AI ( or "superintelligence" ) industry. In its announcement, Nvidia's board said that it has "no reason to believe" that either national security or company secrets were compromised. It also said that Huang "fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it," and that the board has "confidence in Jensen and his leadership team." The investigation will be conducted by independent directors working with outside legal counsel. In response to earlier reports about the CEO's relationship with Alice Huang, Nvidia had said that the pair's interactions were "not unusual," and that the company does not share classified information with customers. Other companies involved in the AI boom have warned employees to be wary of possible spies , including those offering sex or romance.

sources.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admits to an affair with a suspected Chinese spy — Jensen apologizes in letter to staff, company board forms independent committee to investigate - Tom's Hardware
passages: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has admitted to having an affair with a woman who is allegedly a Chinese spy.
His apology came in a letter to Nvidia staff, which you can read in full below.

The board says it has no reason to believe sensitive corporate information or U.S. national security was compromised, but the company intends to examine all available information to determine what happened.
"A committee of independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel, will oversee the investigation," a statement by Nvidia's BoD reads.
The suspected Chinese intelligence operation targeting Jensen has not been independently confirmed as a fact.

The relationship is alleged to follow the typical "honeypot" strategy, wherein foreign intelligence agencies use operatives to ensnare targets into romantic relationships to steal information and influence their decision-making.
Jensen's full letter to staff reads as follows: To my colleagues at NVIDIA, I owe my family and all of you an apology.

The company has been on the radar for smuggling restricted hardware to China since at least 2025: Megaspeed has been accused of smuggling $2 billion worth of AI chips into China via its subsidiary Speedmatrix.

In June 2018, Intel chief executive Brian Krzanich resigned after an internal investigation, assisted by external legal counsel, confirmed that he had engaged in a consensual romantic relationship with an Intel employee, which violated the company's non-fraternization policy applicable to all managers.
For now, it remains unclear if Jensen will meet a similar fate and lose control of the company he founded.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has admitted to having an affair with a woman who is allegedly a Chinese spy. His apology came in a letter to Nvidia staff, which you can read in full below. Nvidia's board of directors released a statement late on Sunday to address the bombshell report that U.S. intelligence believes Huang had an affair with a Chinese spy . The board says it has no reason to believe sensitive corporate information or U.S. national security was compromised, but the company intends to examine all available information to determine what happened. The BoD claims it is fully confident in Jensen Huang and his leadership team. Huang, who has been married to his wife, Lori Huang, for 41 years, says he fully supports the investigation. "A committee of independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel, will oversee the investigation," a statement by Nvidia's BoD reads. "The Board prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of Nvidia and its shareholders. […] Jensen fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it." On Friday, the first reporting emerged claiming U.S. intelligence agencies believe Huang had a romantic relationship with Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed who was allegedly recruited by China's Ministry of State Security (MSS) to gather information and help Chinese companies obtain restricted AI GPUs. The company has been on the radar for smuggling restricted hardware to China since at least 2025: Megaspeed has been accused of smuggling $2 billion worth of AI chips into China via its subsidiary Speedmatrix. To my colleagues at NVIDIA, I owe my family and all of you an apology. Nvidia has strenuously rejected suggestions of improper dealings, saying that its CEO regularly meets thousands of customers and that these interactions do not involve sensitive corporate information or national security secrets. Chinese officials have also dismissed the espionage allegations as unfounded. The suspected Chinese intelligence operation targeting Jensen has not been independently confirmed as a fact. The relationship is alleged to follow the typical "honeypot" strategy, wherein foreign intelligence agencies use operatives to ensnare targets into romantic relationships to steal information and influence their decision-making. Huang has been an outspoken critic of those opposed to limiting the supply of AI GPUs to China. Huang recently expressed his opinion that the label 'China hawk' is not a badge of honor Americans should wear; it is really 'a badge of shame.' Huang also said it "doesn’t have to be all us or them. It could be us and them," drawing fire from others in the administration and other tech companies, including the CEO of Palantir . My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry. Throughout my life, my family has given me love and support. They deserve my honesty and loyalty. Instead, I let them down and damaged the life we built together. I take full responsibility for what I did and the hurt I caused, and I accept the criticism that comes with it. To my wife and family: I love you. I know an apology cannot undo what I have done. I hope our family will heal and that, over time, I can earn back your trust." In June 2018, Intel chief executive Brian Krzanich resigned after an internal investigation, assisted by external legal counsel, confirmed that he had engaged in a consensual romantic relationship with an Intel employee, which violated the company's non-fraternization policy applicable to all managers. Krzanich, who had led Intel since 2013, also stepped down from the company's board, while then-chief financial officer Robert Swan took over as interim CEO. For now, it remains unclear if Jensen will meet a similar fate and lose control of the company he founded. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry. Throughout my life, my family has given me love and support. They deserve my honesty and loyalty. Instead, I let them down and damaged the life we built together. I take full responsibility for what I did and the hurt I caused, and I accept the criticism that comes with it. To my wife and family: I love you. I know an apology cannot undo what I have done. I hope our family will heal and that, over time, I can earn back your trust. To my colleagues at NVIDIA, including those I have worked alongside for decades, and to our board, partners, and shareholders around the world: you deserve better from me. Leading NVIDIA is the privilege of my life. My responsibility is to serve you and be worthy of your trust. I have fallen short of that responsibility. I am fully committed to NVIDIA and will work to earn back your confidence. Regarding the national security concerns raised in news reports, NVIDIA’s Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation. I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. A committee of independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel, will oversee the investigation. The Board prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders. While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information. Jensen fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has admitted to having an affair with a woman who is allegedly a Chinese spy.

sources.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admits to an affair with a suspected Chinese spy — Jensen apologizes in letter to staff, company board forms independent committee to investigate - Tom's Hardware
passages: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has admitted to having an affair with a woman who is allegedly a Chinese spy.
His apology came in a letter to Nvidia staff, which you can read in full below.

The board says it has no reason to believe sensitive corporate information or U.S. national security was compromised, but the company intends to examine all available information to determine what happened.
"A committee of independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel, will oversee the investigation," a statement by Nvidia's BoD reads.
The suspected Chinese intelligence operation targeting Jensen has not been independently confirmed as a fact.

The relationship is alleged to follow the typical "honeypot" strategy, wherein foreign intelligence agencies use operatives to ensnare targets into romantic relationships to steal information and influence their decision-making.
Jensen's full letter to staff reads as follows: To my colleagues at NVIDIA, I owe my family and all of you an apology.

The company has been on the radar for smuggling restricted hardware to China since at least 2025: Megaspeed has been accused of smuggling $2 billion worth of AI chips into China via its subsidiary Speedmatrix.

In June 2018, Intel chief executive Brian Krzanich resigned after an internal investigation, assisted by external legal counsel, confirmed that he had engaged in a consensual romantic relationship with an Intel employee, which violated the company's non-fraternization policy applicable to all managers.
For now, it remains unclear if Jensen will meet a similar fate and lose control of the company he founded.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has admitted to having an affair with a woman who is allegedly a Chinese spy. His apology came in a letter to Nvidia staff, which you can read in full below. Nvidia's board of directors released a statement late on Sunday to address the bombshell report that U.S. intelligence believes Huang had an affair with a Chinese spy . The board says it has no reason to believe sensitive corporate information or U.S. national security was compromised, but the company intends to examine all available information to determine what happened. The BoD claims it is fully confident in Jensen Huang and his leadership team. Huang, who has been married to his wife, Lori Huang, for 41 years, says he fully supports the investigation. "A committee of independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel, will oversee the investigation," a statement by Nvidia's BoD reads. "The Board prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of Nvidia and its shareholders. […] Jensen fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it." On Friday, the first reporting emerged claiming U.S. intelligence agencies believe Huang had a romantic relationship with Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed who was allegedly recruited by China's Ministry of State Security (MSS) to gather information and help Chinese companies obtain restricted AI GPUs. The company has been on the radar for smuggling restricted hardware to China since at least 2025: Megaspeed has been accused of smuggling $2 billion worth of AI chips into China via its subsidiary Speedmatrix. To my colleagues at NVIDIA, I owe my family and all of you an apology. Nvidia has strenuously rejected suggestions of improper dealings, saying that its CEO regularly meets thousands of customers and that these interactions do not involve sensitive corporate information or national security secrets. Chinese officials have also dismissed the espionage allegations as unfounded. The suspected Chinese intelligence operation targeting Jensen has not been independently confirmed as a fact. The relationship is alleged to follow the typical "honeypot" strategy, wherein foreign intelligence agencies use operatives to ensnare targets into romantic relationships to steal information and influence their decision-making. Huang has been an outspoken critic of those opposed to limiting the supply of AI GPUs to China. Huang recently expressed his opinion that the label 'China hawk' is not a badge of honor Americans should wear; it is really 'a badge of shame.' Huang also said it "doesn’t have to be all us or them. It could be us and them," drawing fire from others in the administration and other tech companies, including the CEO of Palantir . My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry. Throughout my life, my family has given me love and support. They deserve my honesty and loyalty. Instead, I let them down and damaged the life we built together. I take full responsibility for what I did and the hurt I caused, and I accept the criticism that comes with it. To my wife and family: I love you. I know an apology cannot undo what I have done. I hope our family will heal and that, over time, I can earn back your trust." In June 2018, Intel chief executive Brian Krzanich resigned after an internal investigation, assisted by external legal counsel, confirmed that he had engaged in a consensual romantic relationship with an Intel employee, which violated the company's non-fraternization policy applicable to all managers. Krzanich, who had led Intel since 2013, also stepped down from the company's board, while then-chief financial officer Robert Swan took over as interim CEO. For now, it remains unclear if Jensen will meet a similar fate and lose control of the company he founded. Jensen's full letter to staff reads as follows: To my colleagues at NVIDIA, I owe my family and all of you an apology. I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry. Throughout my life, my family has given me love and support. They deserve my honesty and loyalty. Instead, I let them down and damaged the life we built together. I take full responsibility for what I did and the hurt I caused, and I accept the criticism that comes with it. To my wife and family: I love you. I know an apology cannot undo what I have done. I hope our family will heal and that, over time, I can earn back your trust. To my colleagues at NVIDIA, including those I have worked alongside for decades, and to our board, partners, and shareholders around the world: you deserve better from me. Leading NVIDIA is the privilege of my life. My responsibility is to serve you and be worthy of your trust. I have fallen short of that responsibility. I am fully committed to NVIDIA and will work to earn back your confidence. Regarding the national security concerns raised in news reports, NVIDIA’s Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation. I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America’s national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American. My family bears no responsibility for my choices. I do. Please give them privacy. The whole statement from Nvidia's Board of Directors reads as follows: The Nvidia Board is initiating an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort. A committee of independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel, will oversee the investigation. The Board prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders. While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information. Jensen fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it.

extraction.body: Nvidia has announced that it is opening an investigation into CEO Jensen Huang and his relationship with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, who was reportedly recruited by China’s Ministry of State Security to spy on the company. A statement posted by the board of directors reads: > The NVIDIA Board is initiating an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort. A committee of independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel, will oversee the investigation. > The Board prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders. While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board’s inquiry will examine all available information. Jensen fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it. > The Board has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team and will provide further updates as appropriate. The New York Times reported last month that Huang had developed a “close relationship” with the Megaspeed executive, which he later admitted was romantic in nature in a memo to the company. Megaspeed is a customer of Nvidia and is the subject of a Commerce Department investigation into whether it was smuggling AI chips to China. The company’s AI chips are viewed as crucial to the US maintaining technological supremacy. President Trump has loosened those restrictions but still bars sales of Nvidia’s most powerful chips to Chinese firms, and the Commerce Department must approve individual firms to handle the chips. Just as importantly, Jensen Huang has gotten quite cozy with Donald Trump, and there is concern about what insights into the administration’s deliberations around AI he may have been privy to. And whether any of that information may have been shared with Alice Huang, and eventually found its way to Beijing.

sources.title: Nvidia will investigate CEO Jensen Huang’s relationship with possible Chinese spy
passages: Nvidia’s board of directors announced Sunday that it’s launching an independent investigation following reports that CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a Chinese spy operation .

In response to earlier reports about the CEO’s relationship with Alice Huang, Nvidia had said that the pair’s interactions were “not unusual,” and that the company does not share classified information with customers.
As the AI race between the United States and China heats up , chips, especially Nvidia’s chips, have been a major focus .
A memo circulating among U.S. policymakers earlier this year claimed that Alice Huang had been recruited by China’s Ministry of State Security to spy on Nvidia’s CEO.
“I owe my family and all of you an apology,” Jensen Huang wrote.
“To my colleagues at NVIDIA, including those I have worked alongside for decades, and to our board, partners, and shareholders around the world: you deserve better from me,” he said.

extraction.body: Nvidia’s board of directors announced Sunday that it’s launching an independent investigation following reports that CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a Chinese spy operation . Nvidia also published a message that Huang sent to the company admitting that he had an affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based chip company Megaspeed (though he didn’t mention her by name). A memo circulating among U.S. policymakers earlier this year claimed that Alice Huang had been recruited by China’s Ministry of State Security to spy on Nvidia’s CEO. “I owe my family and all of you an apology,” Jensen Huang wrote. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.” Huang added that he’d “fallen short” of his responsibility to the company. “To my colleagues at NVIDIA, including those I have worked alongside for decades, and to our board, partners, and shareholders around the world: you deserve better from me,” he said. As the AI race between the United States and China heats up , chips, especially Nvidia’s chips, have been a major focus . Huang also seems to have a close relationship with President Donald Trump , who’s been a cheerleader of the AI ( or “superintelligence” ) industry. In its announcement, Nvidia’s board said that it has “no reason to believe” that either national security or company secrets were compromised. It also said that Huang “fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it,” and that the board has “confidence in Jensen and his leadership team.” The investigation will be conducted by independent directors working with outside legal counsel. In response to earlier reports about the CEO’s relationship with Alice Huang, Nvidia had said that the pair’s interactions were “not unusual,” and that the company does not share classified information with customers. Other companies involved in the AI boom have warned employees to be wary of possible spies , including those offering sex or romance. extraction.body: Nvidia on Sunday said it has opened an investigation into co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with a businesswoman who intelligence agencies said is a Chinese spy . "Today's news will not slow NVIDIA. Jensen is committed to continuing to lead NVIDIA as CEO without interruption," the company told CNBC in a statement. Below is a staff email from Huang obtained by CNBC and a statement released Sunday about the investigation from Nvidia's board of directors. To my colleagues at NVIDIA, I owe my family and all of you an apology. I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry. Throughout my life, my family has given me love and support. They deserve my honesty and loyalty. Instead, I let them down and damaged the life we built together. I take full responsibility for what I did and the hurt I caused, and I accept the criticism that comes with it. To my wife and family: I love you. I know an apology cannot undo what I have done. I hope our family will heal and that, over time, I can earn back your trust. To my colleagues at NVIDIA, including those I have worked alongside for decades, and to our board, partners, and shareholders around the world: you deserve better from me. Leading NVIDIA is the privilege of my life. My responsibility is to serve you and be worthy of your trust. I have fallen short of that responsibility. I am fully committed to NVIDIA and will work to earn back your confidence. Regarding the national security concerns raised in news reports, NVIDIA's Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation. I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America's national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American. My family bears no responsibility for my choices. I do. Please give them privacy. — Jensen The NVIDIA Board is initiating an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort. A committee of independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel, will oversee the investigation. The Board prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders. While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information. Jensen fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it. The Board has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team and will provide further updates as appropriate. US chip giant Nvidia faces fresh scrutiny after its board launched an independent investigation into reports that chief executive Jensen Huang was targeted by a suspected Chinese espionage operation, raising questions about corporate security and the company's international business interests.

The investigation 's outcome could have implications for Nvidia's African operations, including AI infrastructure projects worth $1 billion in Egypt and $1.2 billion in Morocco, alongside developments in South Africa.

Although no project delays have been reported, the controversy raises concerns over data security, corporate governance and the potential exposure of Nvidia's advanced AI technology to foreign intelligence.

In a statement issued on November 8, 2026, Nvidia's board announced that independent directors, assisted by external legal advisers, would investigate reports that Huang had been targeted by foreign intelligence.
"The Board prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders," the company said.
However, the board stressed that it had "no reason to believe" national security or company secrets had been compromised.
The investigation follows reports that Huang had an intimate relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed.

According to The New York Times , US intelligence officials suspected Alice Huang of being recruited by China's Ministry of State Security to gather information about Nvidia's operations, although the allegations remain unproven and no disclosure of sensitive information has been confirmed.

The case has drawn attention amid growing competition between Washington and Beijing over advanced AI chips, with Nvidia's processors at the centre of US restrictions on semiconductor exports to China.

Concerns over the alleged espionage operation had reportedly reached senior US officials months earlier, when Secretary of State Marco Rubio warned members of President Donald Trump's administration about the suspected security threat.
Following the revelations, Huang acknowledged having an extramarital affair and apologised to his family, colleagues and shareholders.
"I owe my family and all of you an apology," he wrote in a message to employees.
"I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry."
Addressing the investigation, Huang added: "I support the investigation and will cooperate fully."
Despite the controversy, Nvidia's board reaffirmed its confidence in Huang and his leadership team
Nvidia's technology is gaining ground across Africa as governments and businesses invest in advanced computing infrastructure, with several major projects announced in 2026.
In Morocco, Nexus Core Systems announced plans in April for a $1.2 billion AI factory near Casablanca, with Nvidia serving as a technology partner.
The facility targets an eventual capacity of 500 megawatts, supporting Morocco's ambitions to expand its advanced computing and digital infrastructure.

Egypt is pursuing a separate data centre project involving Cassava Technologies, the pan-African technology company founded by Zimbabwean billionaire Strive Masiyiwa, alongside Vodafone Business and Elsewedy Electric.
Announced in September, the development could attract up to $1 billion in investment at full capacity and includes a sovereign AI facility designed to use Nvidia technology.

South Africa has also attracted investment in Nvidia-powered infrastructure. In August, Stratos Lab, Ecoblox and Digital Parks Africa announced plans for a $50 million AI cloud project involving more than 400 Nvidia graphics processing units.
Together, these projects underscore Nvidia's growing importance to Africa's AI ambitions, placing its leadership and security practices under greater scrutiny as the investigation unfolds.
However, neither Nvidia nor its African partners has reported disruptions to chip supplies, financing or construction, with no indication that the company's expansion plans have been affected.

Huang, 63, said he is fully cooperating with the investigation. He will continue as the chipmaker's CEO pending the results of the probe. The stunning admission follows a series of reports that Nvidia's leader was targeted by former Megaspeed International executive Alice Huang, who the US government suspects was recruited by a Chinese spy agency. The CEO had previously denied he had anything but a "normal" relationship with the woman. The board investigation will address reports that the chip magnate "has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort," the company said in its statement. "While the board has no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, the board's inquiry will examine all available information." In his memo, Huang said he will support the investigation. "I love our country and our company, and I am committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America's national security," he said. The incident has cast doubt over the future of a man who is central to the artificial intelligence boom. Nvidia's co-founder — a leader famous for his hands-on and tireless management style — built the maker of graphics cards into arguably the world's most important technology company. Nvidia sells the advanced components central to artificial intelligence systems, and the executive has taken on the role of chief evangelist for the spread of AI technology. The Santa Clara, California-based company has no public succession plan, and there is no obvious heir apparent for Huang. He has repeatedly said he wants to continue in his role for decades and has created an informal organizational structure around him that eschews a conventional hierarchy. Instead, his direct reports are tasked with rapidly implementing his decisions. Huang has said that this system gives his company the flexibility to react to rapid changes in technology and remain agile. But it's also created a situation where there's no replacement ready to step in and take over Huang's relentless schedule. Concerns that sensitive information might leak via Nvidia's contacts with China have fueled calls for investigations and greater scrutiny of Huang and the company, ratcheting pressure in what has already been a difficult geopolitical balancing act. While Nvidia is allowed to ship a limited range of products to China under a licensing program granted by the current Trump administration, Beijing has restricted imports of the chips — an impasse that continues to curb the chipmaker's sales in the world's second-largest economy. Investors have poured money into Nvidia, which reports earnings later this month, betting it will continue to be the main beneficiary of runaway spending on AI infrastructure. The company reached a record market capitalization of nearly $5.8 trillion in October. That has slipped below $5 trillion, however, weighed down by concern about the sustainability of AI infrastructure build-out. Megaspeed, based in Singapore, has been accused of breaking US export restrictions and smuggling Nvidia chips to China. Huang had told Bloomberg that his contacts with Megaspeed employees were typical of business relationships he has with many Chinese customers and executives. To my wife and family: I love you. I know an apology cannot undo what I have done. I hope our family will heal and that, over time, I can earn back your trust. To my colleagues at NVIDIA, including those I have worked alongside for decades, and to our board, partners, and shareholders around the world: you deserve better from me. Leading NVIDIA is the privilege of my life. My responsibility is to serve you and be worthy of your trust. I have fallen short of that responsibility. I am fully committed to NVIDIA and will work to earn back your confidence. Regarding the national security concerns raised in news reports, NVIDIA's Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation. I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company, and I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America's national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American. My family bears no responsibility for my choices. I do. Please give them privacy. An Nvidia spokesperson said that Huang was committed to continuing as CEO of Nvidia without interruption. The allegations come as Nvidia has become the center of a trade dispute between China and the U.S. as AI is seen as increasingly critical to national security. U.S. intelligence agencies have expressed concerns that the woman, Alice Huang, who is affiliated with a cloud company and an Nvidia customer called Megaspeed, has been passing information to Beijing, according to reports in The New York Times and the Financial Times. Huang told Nvidia staff in an email on Sunday that he had an affair with the woman and that Nvidia's board of directors had opened an independent investigation into the spying allegations. "I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did," Huang wrote in the message. "I am deeply sorry." An Nvidia spokesperson said that Huang was committed to continuing as CEO of Nvidia without interruption. In a statement, the Nvidia board said it would investigate the allegations that Huang had been the target of a foreign intelligence effort. "While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information," Nvidia's board said in a statement. Read Huang's email to Nvidia employees and the company board of directors' statement here . The allegations come as Nvidia has become the center of a trade dispute between China and the U.S. as AI is seen as increasingly critical to national security. The U.S. restricts exports of Nvidia's most advanced AI chips to China, though it has approved exports of certain older, slower models. Megaspeed, which Ms. Huang is affiliated with, has been accused of helping restricted Chinese companies acquire Nvidia AI chips. Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) launched a new version of Siri just last month, and it's undoubtedly the best version of the personal agent the company has ever released.

Siri can now interact like other artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots by answering more in-depth questions; it also has on-screen awareness and more personal context than before because it can search through photos, emails, and texts.
Most of my personal devices are Apple products, and I've been less than enthused by Siri for years now.
The latest update was a big leap forward, but it essentially caught Apple up with where OpenAI's ChatGPT and Anthropic's Claude were several years ago.
If Apple is in the same place it is now a year from now, after the next iteration of Siri has presumably debuted, Apple's AI software miss could turn into a hardware sales problem.
But as helpful as all of this is, just a few weeks after its launch, Siri still feels dated.

But as helpful as all of this is, just a few weeks after its launch, Siri still feels dated. Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue » With the recent launch of Meta Platforms ' (NASDAQ: META) popular Muse app , which can autonomously complete personal tasks such as booking a flight and shopping online, it's clear that Siri still doesn't measure up. That's a problem for Apple -- and I think it's one the company can solve. But there's a lot at stake if it keeps getting agentic AI wrong. Most of my personal devices are Apple products, and I've been less than enthused by Siri for years now. The latest update was a big leap forward, but it essentially caught Apple up with where OpenAI's ChatGPT and Anthropic's Claude were several years ago. Meta's Muse easily helps users with all sorts of tasks, including booking flights, reserving tables at restaurants, ordering groceries, buying clothes online, and more. It's the type of personal AI assistant that many tech companies have talked about for years, finally built into a simple app. Muse has reached the top of Apple's App Store and has more than 3 million weekly users. That rapid adoption is a good sign that consumers want these capabilities, and there are some important reasons Apple should take notice. The bulk of Apple's revenue -- around 50% -- comes from selling its high-margin iPhones. The margins have taken a bit of a hit recently because of soaring memory prices, but management still estimates gross margins will be around 47%. For decades, Apple has paired high-end devices with top-notch software that consumers mostly love. But Muse and other agents could chip away at this sentiment by offering superior capabilities. Bank of America analyst Wamsi Mohan is concerned about this threat. Mohan said in an investor note last month that Muse could cut into Apple's services revenue by completing online transactions outside of Apple's ecosystem. What's more, if more consumers view Muse as essential to their daily routines, they could shift their smartphone buying habits away from expensive iPhones and toward cheaper Android devices that run Muse just as well. It's still too early to tell whether that will happen, but as users grow more accustomed to highly capable AI agents, paying premium prices for Apple hardware without robust AI built in may not make sense for many smartphone buyers. The biggest hurdle for Muse, and Apple's biggest advantage, is that most users don't trust Meta with their data. A recent Oppenheimer survey found that just 8% of respondents said they trust Meta with their passwords. In contrast, 28% of respondents said they would trust Apple with their passwords. Trust isn't the only factor in winning the agentic AI space, but it's a start. The next step is, of course, for Apple to design Siri to work better within third-party apps to complete autonomous tasks. The real problem for Apple isn't the technical know-how; it may be whether Apple's management believes the company needs to make such a leap with Siri to stay relevant. The latest version of Siri is a step in the right direction, but as an Apple shareholder myself, I wonder how long it will be before Siri catches up to other AI agents. If Apple is in the same place it is now a year from now, after the next iteration of Siri has presumably debuted, Apple's AI software miss could turn into a hardware sales problem. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout, a massive technology build-out that Google's CEO says could be more profound than fire or electricity. While everyone watches the chip designers, one "backbone" company provides the critical technology that Nvidia and AMD literally cannot function without. Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) launched a new version of Siri just last month, and it's undoubtedly the best version of the personal agent the company has ever released.

Siri can now interact like other artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots by answering more in-depth questions; it also has on-screen awareness and more personal context than before because it can search through photos, emails, and texts.
Most of my personal devices are Apple products, and I've been less than enthused by Siri for years now.
The latest update was a big leap forward, but it essentially caught Apple up with where OpenAI's ChatGPT and Anthropic's Claude were several years ago.
If Apple is in the same place it is now a year from now, after the next iteration of Siri has presumably debuted, Apple's AI software miss could turn into a hardware sales problem.
But as helpful as all of this is, just a few weeks after its launch, Siri still feels dated.

With the recent launch of Meta Platforms ' (NASDAQ: META) popular Muse app , which can autonomously complete personal tasks such as booking a flight and shopping online, it's clear that Siri still doesn't measure up.

sources.title: Apple CEO Pushes Siri Agent Overhaul to Match OpenAI, Meta
passages: Apple CEO John Ternus is putting intense pressure on AI chief Craig Federighi to transform Siri into a full-fledged agentic assistant capable of competing with OpenAI's Dots and Meta's Muse, according to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman.
If third-party apps optimize for OpenAI and Meta agents first, Apple risks becoming a second-class citizen in the AI ecosystem it desperately wants to control.

While Federighi's team managed to ship a working version of Siri AI on what insiders describe as an "incredibly short timeline," Apple executives privately admit they're not keeping pace with rivals who've already deployed AI agents capable of autonomous, multi-step tasks.
Meta, meanwhile, has been aggressively rolling out Muse across its family of apps, giving billions of users access to agentic capabilities.
The company needs Siri to become genuinely useful - not just incrementally better - to keep developers building for Apple Intelligence first.
Users expect agents that anticipate needs, coordinate complex workflows, and actually save time - capabilities that require fundamentally different architectures than what Siri was built on.
Apple's internal urgency around Siri signals a broader shift in how the company views AI competition.
But relying on OpenAI for core assistant functionality undermines Apple's ecosystem lock-in and puts user data in third-party hands - exactly the scenario Cupertino has spent decades avoiding.
Apple is scrambling to catch up in the agentic AI wars.
The pressure from Ternus suggests Apple views agentic AI as existential, not incremental.

For users, the promise of fine-grained app control and deeper automation sounds compelling, but the real question is whether Apple can deliver transformative agentic capabilities while maintaining the privacy and polish that define its brand.

extraction.body: Apple CEO John Ternus is putting intense pressure on AI chief Craig Federighi to transform Siri into a full-fledged agentic assistant capable of competing with OpenAI's Dots and Meta's Muse, according to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman. While Federighi delivered a functional Siri AI on a compressed timeline, the company knows it's falling behind in the race to build powerful AI agents that can autonomously handle complex tasks across apps and services. Apple is scrambling to catch up in the agentic AI wars. CEO John Ternus isn't satisfied with Siri's current trajectory and is leaning hard on software chief Craig Federighi to deliver something that can actually go toe-to-toe with OpenAI's Dots and Meta's Muse, Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reports. While Federighi's team managed to ship a working version of Siri AI on what insiders describe as an "incredibly short timeline," Apple executives privately admit they're not keeping pace with rivals who've already deployed AI agents capable of autonomous, multi-step tasks. It's a rare admission of vulnerability from a company that typically sets the industry tempo. Two significant capability upgrades are headed to Siri in the coming months, according to Gurman's sources. The first will give the assistant granular control over Apple's native apps - think rotating and cropping images directly in Photos, organizing Safari tabs by topic, or managing complex Mail workflows without constant user prompting. OpenAI just closed an $11 billion funding round that values the ChatGPT maker at $1.25 trillion, cementing its position as the world's most valuable startup. Its Dots agent can already handle sophisticated tasks like booking travel, managing schedules, and coordinating across multiple services with minimal human intervention. Meta, meanwhile, has been aggressively rolling out Muse across its family of apps, giving billions of users access to agentic capabilities. Apple's challenge is architectural as much as it is competitive. The company built its reputation on tightly controlled, privacy-first experiences, but modern AI agents demand access to vast amounts of user data and cross-app coordination to function effectively. Federighi's team is essentially trying to build a competitive agent while maintaining Apple's privacy guardrails - a technical high-wire act that's proving harder than anticipated. The pressure from Ternus suggests Apple views agentic AI as existential, not incremental. The company recently began integrating ChatGPT support into its HomeView smart hub, signaling a willingness to partner with rivals when its own technology lags. But relying on OpenAI for core assistant functionality undermines Apple's ecosystem lock-in and puts user data in third-party hands - exactly the scenario Cupertino has spent decades avoiding. Industry observers note that Apple's historical playbook - wait, watch, then perfect - doesn't work when competitors are shipping transformative capabilities to hundreds of millions of users every quarter. Amazon just launched its own text-to-shop Alexa feature after blocking Meta's Muse from its platform, showing how quickly the agentic landscape is fragmenting. The internal roadmap acceleration also reflects concerns about developer momentum. If third-party apps optimize for OpenAI and Meta agents first, Apple risks becoming a second-class citizen in the AI ecosystem it desperately wants to control. The company needs Siri to become genuinely useful - not just incrementally better - to keep developers building for Apple Intelligence first. What remains unclear is whether Apple can compress its development timeline enough to matter. The company's methodical approach to shipping polished products has served it well in hardware, but software moves faster, and AI moves faster still. Federighi delivered functional Siri AI quickly, but "functional" isn't the bar anymore. Users expect agents that anticipate needs, coordinate complex workflows, and actually save time - capabilities that require fundamentally different architectures than what Siri was built on. The coming months will reveal whether Apple's internal pressure translates to external progress. Ternus isn't just asking for iterative improvements; he's demanding a competitive agent that can stand alongside the industry's best. That's a tall order for a company that's spent the past year playing catch-up while rivals sprint ahead. Apple's internal urgency around Siri signals a broader shift in how the company views AI competition. This isn't about adding features to maintain parity - it's about building an agent capable of genuinely competing with OpenAI and Meta's offerings before the window closes. For users, the promise of fine-grained app control and deeper automation sounds compelling, but the real question is whether Apple can deliver transformative agentic capabilities while maintaining the privacy and polish that define its brand. The pressure from Ternus suggests the company knows it's running out of time to prove it can.

The key insight: Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reported on November 8 that Apple wants to make Siri more agent-like, possibly as early as next year in Gurman’s view, contrasting Siri’s request-based actions with ChatGPT Dots, Meta Muse and Grok, which Gurman said keep working between conversations. Apple also gave engineers six weeks of coding instead of four in the first iOS 28 milestone, which by our arithmetic is 50% more coding time in that stage. Gurman wrote that today’s Siri AI “can properly answer questions, write emails and text messages, set reminders, pull information from the open web, serve up news and take basic actions inside apps”. Gurman described its biggest development this year as the ability to draw context from what is on a user’s display and from private information on Apple devices, such as emails and text messages. The iOS 27.3 beta adds precise control over Apple ’s own apps, Gurman reported, with examples including organising Safari tabs, sorting Files folders, unsending an iMessage and multistep Photos edits. Gurman wrote that support for Apple ’s apps “could come as early as December” and that third-party app support probably won’t arrive until the spring. Our earlier piece reported Apple opening Siri AI to any app . Gurman also posted that Apple is changing how it develops iOS 28, iPadOS 28 and macOS 28, giving engineers more time to explore and build new features before locking them in. The newsletter puts the change at six weeks of coding and two of convergence in the first milestone, instead of four and four. Apple is exploring turning Siri into a background AI agent similar to OpenAI ’s ChatGPT Dots as part of an iOS 28 shake-up, according to Bloomberg. Apple is still delivering the Siri overhaul it promised years ago. Now it is already exploring the architecture that could make that version look obsolete. Choblin29 relayed the Bloomberg report and added a view that Apple is exploring an architecture that could make its promised Siri overhaul look obsolete. That framing is the poster’s own; the newsletter says Apple wants to go in the agent direction and that the in-app actions promised in 2024 are still arriving in iOS 27.3. An X user posting as cryptopunk7213 (Ejaaz) shared a personal take on Gurman’s report at 17:07 UTC on 8 November. The post describes the reported feature as letting third-party apps integrate with Siri so it can act across apps, and argues that Apple’s installed base of devices is an advantage; that argument and the 3.5 billion devices figure are the poster’s, not Bloomberg’s. Gurman wrote that these features are “nothing close to what you can do with something like ChatGPT ’s Dots, Meta ’s Muse and Elon Musk ’s Grok”. Gurman listed what those agents do: they “can remember projects and preferences over time, monitor connected sources for changes, proactively surface information, and decide when to pause and resume work”. In Gurman’s summary, Siri “can now execute more complicated requests and integrate more deeply with third-party software ”, while Dots, Muse and Grok “can keep track of goals, determine what needs to happen next and continue pursuing objectives without the user initiating every individual step”. Apple ultimately wants to go in that direction, Gurman wrote, citing people Gurman spoke to. Apple CEO John Ternus said on the company’s earnings call, as quoted by Bloomberg, that Siri is “primarily request-based today” but “built on a modern orchestrator-driven architecture that gives us real room to expand its capabilities over time”. Ternus added that Apple wants agentic features done “in a way that protects security and privacy”. Our earlier piece covered Ternus pressing Federighi on AI , including the separate gap Gurman flagged in computer use. Gurman called a feature Apple showed at WWDC 2026 its “first truly agent-like iOS feature”: software that would analyse passwords saved to a user’s Apple account, identify weak or compromised credentials, and go from website to website changing them. The feature appeared early in the iOS 27 beta cycle before quietly disappearing, and Apple’s iOS marketing site still says it will arrive in the future, Gurman reported. Apple traditionally splits each year’s operating-system work into three milestones, M1, M2 and M3, each running eight weeks of four weeks of coding and four weeks of convergence, Gurman reported. For M1 of this cycle, covering Bell (iOS 28 and iPadOS 28) and Poppy (macOS 28), engineers got six weeks of coding, exploration and feature development and two weeks of convergence, according to the newsletter. Employees say they like the change, which creates more time to come up with ideas before locking them in, Gurman wrote. Development of the M2 milestone kicks off on Monday, and that is the period when Apple will start to finalise what it plans to include, according to the report. Our coverage has also included Anthropic’s Claude ‘Dreams’ memory research and Perplexity’s launch of Teammates . As we read the newsletter, the gap Gurman describes is less about what Siri can do in a single request and more about whether it can hold a goal over time and act without being asked. As we read the iOS 28 change, giving engineers six weeks to explore before converging is a process signal that Apple is making room for new features before it locks the 2027 releases in. As we read Ternus’s quoted remarks, Apple frames agentic features around user awareness, security and privacy, which is the constraint Gurman sets against the speed of ChatGPT Dots, Muse and Grok. Apple wants to move Siri toward agent-style work, and Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman wrote in the Power On newsletter on November 8 that Gurman believes the company “could make Siri more like an agent as early as next year”. Gurman contrasted Siri in iOS 27.3, which carries out actions when a user gives a command, with ChatGPT ’s Dots, Meta ’s Muse and Elon Musk ’s Grok, which Gurman said can be handed an ongoing responsibility and continue working between conversations.

The same newsletter reported that Apple changed how it builds its 2027 operating systems. In the first development milestone for iOS 28, iPadOS 28 and macOS 28, engineers got six weeks of coding, exploration and feature development and two weeks of convergence, instead of the usual four and four, according to Bloomberg. By our arithmetic, that is 50% more coding time and half the convergence time in that stage.
An evergreen Business Engineer explainer on AI agents. It teaches the general idea only and does not discuss Siri.

The key insight: Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reported on November 8 that Apple wants to make Siri more agent-like, possibly as early as next year in Gurman’s view, contrasting Siri’s request-based actions with ChatGPT Dots, Meta Muse and Grok, which Gurman said keep working between conversations. Apple also gave engineers six weeks of coding instead of four in the first iOS 28 milestone, which by our arithmetic is 50% more coding time in that stage.

Gurman wrote that today’s Siri AI “can properly answer questions, write emails and text messages, set reminders, pull information from the open web, serve up news and take basic actions inside apps”. Gurman described its biggest development this year as the ability to draw context from what is on a user’s display and from private information on Apple devices, such as emails and text messages.

The iOS 27.3 beta adds precise control over Apple ’s own apps, Gurman reported, with examples including organising Safari tabs, sorting Files folders, unsending an iMessage and multistep Photos edits. Gurman wrote that support for Apple ’s apps “could come as early as December” and that third-party app support probably won’t arrive until the spring. Our earlier piece reported Apple opening Siri AI to any app .

Gurman also posted that Apple is changing how it develops iOS 28, iPadOS 28 and macOS 28, giving engineers more time to explore and build new features before locking them in. The newsletter puts the change at six weeks of coding and two of convergence in the first milestone, instead of four and four.

Apple is exploring turning Siri into a background AI agent similar to OpenAI ’s ChatGPT Dots as part of an iOS 28 shake-up, according to Bloomberg. Apple is still delivering the Siri overhaul it promised years ago. Now it is already exploring the architecture that could make that version look obsolete.

Choblin29 relayed the Bloomberg report and added a view that Apple is exploring an architecture that could make its promised Siri overhaul look obsolete. That framing is the poster’s own; the newsletter says Apple wants to go in the agent direction and that the in-app actions promised in 2024 are still arriving in iOS 27.3.

Apple finally stepping up to compete in AI with a personal AI agent that rivals Meta Muse, grok bot etc. few thoughts: – the new feature would allow 3rd-party apps to integrate siri. which means siri can perform actions, pull context through every app on your phone. that’s pretty sick. – despite being behind in AI, apple has a huge advantage: 3.5 billion devices people love and use everyday – but at the same time siri right now sucks, is incapable of doing even 30% of the things frontier LLMs can do. it can’t even use a computer. – compare this to muse, dots or grok bot that can work autonomously 24/7, self-improving the more you use it AND have access to their own computer. they’re miles ahead. imo apple has to balance delivering quickly (& aggressively) on AI without causing a major security breach. their whole thing is trust and privacy. that’s the challenge ternus will face.

An X user posting as cryptopunk7213 (Ejaaz) shared a personal take on Gurman’s report at 17:07 UTC on 8 November. The post describes the reported feature as letting third-party apps integrate with Siri so it can act across apps, and argues that Apple’s installed base of devices is an advantage; that argument and the 3.5 billion devices figure are the poster’s, not Bloomberg’s.

Gurman wrote that these features are “nothing close to what you can do with something like ChatGPT ’s Dots, Meta ’s Muse and Elon Musk ’s Grok”. Gurman listed what those agents do: they “can remember projects and preferences over time, monitor connected sources for changes, proactively surface information, and decide when to pause and resume work”.

In Gurman’s summary, Siri “can now execute more complicated requests and integrate more deeply with third-party software ”, while Dots, Muse and Grok “can keep track of goals, determine what needs to happen next and continue pursuing objectives without the user initiating every individual step”. Apple ultimately wants to go in that direction, Gurman wrote, citing people Gurman spoke to.

Apple CEO John Ternus said on the company’s earnings call, as quoted by Bloomberg, that Siri is “primarily request-based today” but “built on a modern orchestrator-driven architecture that gives us real room to expand its capabilities over time”. Ternus added that Apple wants agentic features done “in a way that protects security and privacy”. Our earlier piece covered Ternus pressing Federighi on AI , including the separate gap Gurman flagged in computer use.

Gurman called a feature Apple showed at WWDC 2026 its “first truly agent-like iOS feature”: software that would analyse passwords saved to a user’s Apple account, identify weak or compromised credentials, and go from website to website changing them. The feature appeared early in the iOS 27 beta cycle before quietly disappearing, and Apple’s iOS marketing site still says it will arrive in the future, Gurman reported.

Apple traditionally splits each year’s operating-system work into three milestones, M1, M2 and M3, each running eight weeks of four weeks of coding and four weeks of convergence, Gurman reported. For M1 of this cycle, covering Bell (iOS 28 and iPadOS 28) and Poppy (macOS 28), engineers got six weeks of coding, exploration and feature development and two weeks of convergence, according to the newsletter.

Employees say they like the change, which creates more time to come up with ideas before locking them in, Gurman wrote. Development of the M2 milestone kicks off on Monday, and that is the period when Apple will start to finalise what it plans to include, according to the report.
Our coverage has also included Anthropic’s Claude ‘Dreams’ memory research and Perplexity’s launch of Teammates .
As we read the newsletter, the gap Gurman describes is less about what Siri can do in a single request and more about whether it can hold a goal over time and act without being asked.
As we read the iOS 28 change, giving engineers six weeks to explore before converging is a process signal that Apple is making room for new features before it locks the 2027 releases in.
As we read Ternus’s quoted remarks, Apple frames agentic features around user awareness, security and privacy, which is the constraint Gurman sets against the speed of ChatGPT Dots, Muse and Grok.
Apple CEO John Ternus on the earnings call, as quoted by Bloomberg

FOR RIVAL AGENT MAKERS Gurman listed what ChatGPT Dots, Meta Muse and Grok do that Siri does not: remember projects, monitor sources, surface information proactively and decide when to pause and resume work.

As we read it, Gurman’s comparison is about that surface: Apple owns the devices and operating systems, while the agent layer users delegate goals to is being built by ChatGPT Dots, Meta Muse and Grok. The essay does not discuss Siri.

coreStoryFacts.text: Trust isn't the only factor in winning the agentic AI space, but it's a start.
The next step is, of course, for Apple to design Siri to work better within third-party apps to complete autonomous tasks.
Yahoo Finance is not a broker-dealer or investment adviser and does not offer securities or cryptocurrencies for sale or facilitate trading.
Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) launched a new version of Siri just last month, and it's undoubtedly the best version of the personal agent the company has ever released.

Siri can now interact like other artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots by answering more in-depth questions; it also has on-screen awareness and more personal context than before because it can search through photos, emails, and texts.
Most of my personal devices are Apple products, and I've been less than enthused by Siri for years now.
The latest update was a big leap forward, but it essentially caught Apple up with where OpenAI's ChatGPT and Anthropic's Claude were several years ago.
If Apple is in the same place it is now a year from now, after the next iteration of Siri has presumably debuted, Apple's AI software miss could turn into a hardware sales problem.
But as helpful as all of this is, just a few weeks after its launch, Siri still feels dated.

With the recent launch of Meta Platforms ' (NASDAQ: META) popular Muse app , which can autonomously complete personal tasks such as booking a flight and shopping online, it's clear that Siri still doesn't measure up.
Apple is expected to push Siri to become more agentic and enable features that will allow it to perform ongoing tasks, not just one-offs.

Apple ultimately wants to go in this direction, I’m told, and I believe the company could make Siri more like an agent as early as next year — not that it has much of a choice, given current consumer and market demands.
Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman says CEO John Ternus is pressuring AI czar Craig Federighi to accelerate the Siri roadmap and deliver a powerful AI agent that can compete with OpenAI’s Dots or Meta’s Muse.
Two significant improvements are expected to be made to Siri in the coming months.
One will give the assistant fine-grained control over Apple’s first-party apps, allowing it to do things like rotate and crop images in Photos and organize Safari tabs.
That would let Siri place an order through Grubhub or book a dinner reservation through OpenTable, for example.

Apple CEO John Ternus is putting intense pressure on AI chief Craig Federighi to transform Siri into a full-fledged agentic assistant capable of competing with OpenAI's Dots and Meta's Muse, according to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman.
If third-party apps optimize for OpenAI and Meta agents first, Apple risks becoming a second-class citizen in the AI ecosystem it desperately wants to control.

While Federighi's team managed to ship a working version of Siri AI on what insiders describe as an "incredibly short timeline," Apple executives privately admit they're not keeping pace with rivals who've already deployed AI agents capable of autonomous, multi-step tasks.
Meta, meanwhile, has been aggressively rolling out Muse across its family of apps, giving billions of users access to agentic capabilities.
The company needs Siri to become genuinely useful - not just incrementally better - to keep developers building for Apple Intelligence first.
Users expect agents that anticipate needs, coordinate complex workflows, and actually save time - capabilities that require fundamentally different architectures than what Siri was built on.
Apple's internal urgency around Siri signals a broader shift in how the company views AI competition.
But relying on OpenAI for core assistant functionality undermines Apple's ecosystem lock-in and puts user data in third-party hands - exactly the scenario Cupertino has spent decades avoiding.

extraction.body: Apple CEO John Ternus is putting intense pressure on AI chief Craig Federighi to transform Siri into a full-fledged agentic assistant capable of competing with OpenAI's Dots and Meta's Muse, according to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman. While Federighi delivered a functional Siri AI on a compressed timeline, the company knows it's falling behind in the race to build powerful AI agents that can autonomously handle complex tasks across apps and services. Apple is scrambling to catch up in the agentic AI wars. CEO John Ternus isn't satisfied with Siri's current trajectory and is leaning hard on software chief Craig Federighi to deliver something that can actually go toe-to-toe with OpenAI's Dots and Meta's Muse, Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reports. While Federighi's team managed to ship a working version of Siri AI on what insiders describe as an "incredibly short timeline," Apple executives privately admit they're not keeping pace with rivals who've already deployed AI agents capable of autonomous, multi-step tasks. It's a rare admission of vulnerability from a company that typically sets the industry tempo. Two significant capability upgrades are headed to Siri in the coming months, according to Gurman's sources. The first will give the assistant granular control over Apple's native apps - think rotating and cropping images directly in Photos, organizing Safari tabs by topic, or managing complex Mail workflows without constant user prompting. OpenAI just closed an $11 billion funding round that values the ChatGPT maker at $1.25 trillion, cementing its position as the world's most valuable startup. Its Dots agent can already handle sophisticated tasks like booking travel, managing schedules, and coordinating across multiple services with minimal human intervention. Meta, meanwhile, has been aggressively rolling out Muse across its family of apps, giving billions of users access to agentic capabilities. Apple's challenge is architectural as much as it is competitive. The company built its reputation on tightly controlled, privacy-first experiences, but modern AI agents demand access to vast amounts of user data and cross-app coordination to function effectively. Federighi's team is essentially trying to build a competitive agent while maintaining Apple's privacy guardrails - a technical high-wire act that's proving harder than anticipated. The pressure from Ternus suggests Apple views agentic AI as existential, not incremental. The company recently began integrating ChatGPT support into its HomeView smart hub, signaling a willingness to partner with rivals when its own technology lags. But relying on OpenAI for core assistant functionality undermines Apple's ecosystem lock-in and puts user data in third-party hands - exactly the scenario Cupertino has spent decades avoiding. Industry observers note that Apple's historical playbook - wait, watch, then perfect - doesn't work when competitors are shipping transformative capabilities to hundreds of millions of users every quarter. Amazon just launched its own text-to-shop Alexa feature after blocking Meta's Muse from its platform, showing how quickly the agentic landscape is fragmenting. The internal roadmap acceleration also reflects concerns about developer momentum. If third-party apps optimize for OpenAI and Meta agents first, Apple risks becoming a second-class citizen in the AI ecosystem it desperately wants to control. The company needs Siri to become genuinely useful - not just incrementally better - to keep developers building for Apple Intelligence first. What remains unclear is whether Apple can compress its development timeline enough to matter. The company's methodical approach to shipping polished products has served it well in hardware, but software moves faster, and AI moves faster still. Federighi delivered functional Siri AI quickly, but "functional" isn't the bar anymore. Users expect agents that anticipate needs, coordinate complex workflows, and actually save time - capabilities that require fundamentally different architectures than what Siri was built on. The coming months will reveal whether Apple's internal pressure translates to external progress. Ternus isn't just asking for iterative improvements; he's demanding a competitive agent that can stand alongside the industry's best. That's a tall order for a company that's spent the past year playing catch-up while rivals sprint ahead. Apple's internal urgency around Siri signals a broader shift in how the company views AI competition. This isn't about adding features to maintain parity - it's about building an agent capable of genuinely competing with OpenAI and Meta's offerings before the window closes. For users, the promise of fine-grained app control and deeper automation sounds compelling, but the real question is whether Apple can deliver transformative agentic capabilities while maintaining the privacy and polish that define its brand. Meta, meanwhile, has been aggressively rolling out Muse across its family of apps, giving billions of users access to agentic capabilities.
Apple's challenge is architectural as much as it is competitive.

passages: The key insight: Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reported on November 8 that Apple wants to make Siri more agent-like, possibly as early as next year in Gurman’s view, contrasting Siri’s request-based actions with ChatGPT Dots, Meta Muse and Grok, which Gurman said keep working between conversations.
Apple also gave engineers six weeks of coding instead of four in the first iOS 28 milestone, which by our arithmetic is 50% more coding time in that stage.
The same newsletter reported that Apple changed how it builds its 2027 operating systems.
Apple has not announced an agentic Siri or a date for one.
We first saw the story in X posts by @markgurman and @choblin29.
Apple is still delivering the Siri overhaul it promised years ago.
Now it is already exploring the architecture that could make that version look obsolete.

Apple CEO John Ternus said on the company’s earnings call, as quoted by Bloomberg, that Siri is “primarily request-based today” but “built on a modern orchestrator-driven architecture that gives us real room to expand its capabilities over time”.
Our earlier piece reported Apple opening Siri AI to any app .

Apple finally stepping up to compete in AI with a personal AI agent that rivals Meta Muse, grok bot etc. few thoughts: – the new feature would allow 3rd-party apps to integrate siri. which means siri can perform actions, pull context through every app on your phone. that’s pretty sick. – despite being behind in AI, apple has a huge advantage: 3.5 billion devices people love and use everyday – but at the same time siri right now sucks, is incapable of doing even 30% of the things frontier LLMs can do. it can’t even use a computer. – compare this to muse, dots or grok bot that can work autonomously 24/7, self-improving the more you use it AND have access to their own computer. they’re miles ahead. imo apple has to balance delivering quickly (& aggressively) on AI without causing a major security breach. their whole thing is trust and privacy. that’s the challenge ternus will face.

In the first development milestone for iOS 28, iPadOS 28 and macOS 28, engineers got six weeks of coding, exploration and feature development and two weeks of convergence, instead of the usual four and four, according to Bloomberg. The key insight: Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reported on November 8 that Apple wants to make Siri more agent-like, possibly as early as next year in Gurman’s view, contrasting Siri’s request-based actions with ChatGPT Dots, Meta Muse and Grok, which Gurman said keep working between conversations. Apple also gave engineers six weeks of coding instead of four in the first iOS 28 milestone, which by our arithmetic is 50% more coding time in that stage. Gurman wrote that today’s Siri AI “can properly answer questions, write emails and text messages, set reminders, pull information from the open web, serve up news and take basic actions inside apps”. Gurman described its biggest development this year as the ability to draw context from what is on a user’s display and from private information on Apple devices, such as emails and text messages. The iOS 27.3 beta adds precise control over Apple ’s own apps, Gurman reported, with examples including organising Safari tabs, sorting Files folders, unsending an iMessage and multistep Photos edits. Gurman wrote that support for Apple ’s apps “could come as early as December” and that third-party app support probably won’t arrive until the spring. Our earlier piece reported Apple opening Siri AI to any app . Gurman also posted that Apple is changing how it develops iOS 28, iPadOS 28 and macOS 28, giving engineers more time to explore and build new features before locking them in. The newsletter puts the change at six weeks of coding and two of convergence in the first milestone, instead of four and four. Apple is exploring turning Siri into a background AI agent similar to OpenAI ’s ChatGPT Dots as part of an iOS 28 shake-up, according to Bloomberg. Apple is still delivering the Siri overhaul it promised years ago. Now it is already exploring the architecture that could make that version look obsolete. Choblin29 relayed the Bloomberg report and added a view that Apple is exploring an architecture that could make its promised Siri overhaul look obsolete. An X user posting as cryptopunk7213 (Ejaaz) shared a personal take on Gurman’s report at 17:07 UTC on 8 November. The post describes the reported feature as letting third-party apps integrate with Siri so it can act across apps, and argues that Apple’s installed base of devices is an advantage; that argument and the 3.5 billion devices figure are the poster’s, not Bloomberg’s. Gurman wrote that these features are “nothing close to what you can do with something like ChatGPT ’s Dots, Meta ’s Muse and Elon Musk ’s Grok”. Gurman listed what those agents do: they “can remember projects and preferences over time, monitor connected sources for changes, proactively surface information, and decide when to pause and resume work”. In Gurman’s summary, Siri “can now execute more complicated requests and integrate more deeply with third-party software ”, while Dots, Muse and Grok “can keep track of goals, determine what needs to happen next and continue pursuing objectives without the user initiating every individual step”. Apple ultimately wants to go in that direction, Gurman wrote, citing people Gurman spoke to. Apple CEO John Ternus said on the company’s earnings call, as quoted by Bloomberg, that Siri is “primarily request-based today” but “built on a modern orchestrator-driven architecture that gives us real room to expand its capabilities over time”. Ternus added that Apple wants agentic features done “in a way that protects security and privacy”. For M1 of this cycle, covering Bell (iOS 28 and iPadOS 28) and Poppy (macOS 28), engineers got six weeks of coding, exploration and feature development and two weeks of convergence, according to the newsletter. Development of the M2 milestone kicks off on Monday, and that is the period when Apple will start to finalise what it plans to include, according to the report. Our coverage has also included Anthropic’s Claude ‘Dreams’ memory research and Perplexity’s launch of Teammates . As we read the newsletter, the gap Gurman describes is less about what Siri can do in a single request and more about whether it can hold a goal over time and act without being asked. As we read the iOS 28 change, giving engineers six weeks to explore before converging is a process signal that Apple is making room for new features before it locks the 2027 releases in. sources.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admits to an affair with a suspected Chinese spy — Jensen apologizes in letter to staff, company board forms independent committee to investigate - Tom's Hardware
passages: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has admitted to having an affair with a woman who is allegedly a Chinese spy.
His apology came in a letter to Nvidia staff, which you can read in full below.

The board says it has no reason to believe sensitive corporate information or U.S. national security was compromised, but the company intends to examine all available information to determine what happened.
"A committee of independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel, will oversee the investigation," a statement by Nvidia's BoD reads.
The suspected Chinese intelligence operation targeting Jensen has not been independently confirmed as a fact.
